summary: Koei Tecmo's camera-based Japanese horror series; preserve the original trilogy's expanded console versions separately from later remakes, and use modern PC remasters where they exist.

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox hardware if emulator compatibility is imperfect.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox original / emulator scaling where compatible

primary.platform: Xbox via xemu or original hardware
primary.why: The Xbox port is the most complete version of the first game, with improved visuals and additional story/gameplay material over the PS2 original.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version through xemu if compatibility is acceptable, or on original Xbox hardware; use PCSX2 only for the original PS2 release.

entries.title: Fatal Frame II: Crimson Butterfly

emulation.notes: Use original Xbox hardware if emulator compatibility is imperfect.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox Director's Cut / emulator scaling where compatible

primary.platform: Xbox via xemu or original hardware
primary.why: The Xbox Director's Cut is the most complete classic version, adding updated graphics, first-person camera option, harder difficulty, costumes, and the Promise ending.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox Director's Cut through xemu if compatible or original Xbox hardware; treat the Wii and 2026 remakes as separate entries.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate with Project Zero 2: Wii Edition or the 2026 full remake; both are separate remake entries.

primary.why: The Tormented is a PS2-only main-series entry with no modern port documented; PCSX2 gives the best practical fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release through PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original PS2 hardware.

primary.why: Real Zero was a mobile Fatal Frame title built around taking real-world photos and collecting superimposed ghost images; its service ended in 2011.
primary.how_to_play: No current official route is documented; treat as an archival defunct mobile-service entry.

entries.title: Fatal Frame: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse

emulation.emulator: None for PC; Dolphin for Wii original
emulation.notes: Use Dolphin/Wii only for original-control comparison.

primary.why: The 2023 remaster gives the formerly Japan-only Wii entry an official worldwide release with updated graphics and new unlockable costumes; PC has the highest fidelity ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC remaster; use Dolphin/Wii only if you specifically want the original Wii Remote control scheme.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remaster reworks controls for modern platforms and adds new costumes.

entries.title: Project Zero 2: Wii Edition

emulation.notes: Use original Wii controls or equivalent motion setup.

primary.platform: Wii via Dolphin or original hardware
primary.why: The Wii remake of Crimson Butterfly updates graphics/gameplay, incorporates Xbox-release content, adds story elements, and adds two endings plus a Haunted House mode.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PAL/Japan Wii release through Dolphin with appropriate controls, or on original Wii hardware; keep it distinct from the 2003 classic and 2026 remake.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not released in North America; do not conflate with the Xbox Director's Cut or 2026 remake.

primary.why: Spirit Camera is a 3DS-only Fatal Frame spin-off built around the system cameras, AR functions, and bundled Diary of Faces booklet.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Nintendo 3DS hardware with the AR booklet; emulation is not the recommended route because camera/AR physical interaction is core to the design.

entries.title: Fatal Frame: Maiden of Black Water

emulation.emulator: None for PC; Cemu for Wii U original
emulation.notes: Use Wii U/Cemu only to compare original GamePad-style play.

primary.why: The 2021 remaster brings the Wii U entry to modern platforms with updated visuals, new costumes, and photo mode; PC has the highest fidelity ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC remaster; use Wii U only if you want the original GamePad-as-Camera-Obscura control concept.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remaster adapts Wii U-specific controls to modern platforms and adds new costumes/photo mode.

entries.title: Fatal Frame II: Crimson Butterfly Remake

primary.why: The 2026 remake is a full modern rebuild with overhauled graphics, sound, controls, new systems, and an additional ending; PC is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PC release; use Switch 2 only if you specifically want its motion-control handheld features.

entries.remaster_caveats: Full remake with new systems and ending; not the same object as the 2003 classic or 2012 Wii remake.
